### Research Question
What is the relationship between late night social media usage and perceived stress score. 

### Hypotheses 
H0 = Late night social media usage does not impact perceived stress score. 
H1 = Late night social media usage does impact perceived stress score. 

### Load database 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
SM_use <- read_csv("C:/Users/kierr/Downloads/Social_media_impact_on_life.csv", 
    col_types = cols(Age = col_number(), 
        Daily_Usage_Hours = col_number(), 
        Weekend_Extra_Hours = col_number(), 
        Sleep_Duration_Hours = col_number(), 
        Sleep_Quality_Score = col_number(), 
        Late_Night_Usage = col_character(), 
        Perceived_Stress_Score = col_number(), 
        Mental_Health_Index = col_number(), 
        Academic_Performance_GPA = col_number()))

View(SM_use)
```

### Normality tests 
Plots a histogram and runs a Shapiro-Wilk test for late night usage of social media, True or False. 
```{r}
# filter databases 
SM_use_LateNight_True <- SM_use %>%
  filter(SM_use$Late_Night_Usage == "True")

SM_use_LateNight_False <- SM_use %>%
  filter(SM_use$Late_Night_Usage == "False")

#plot histograms
SM_use_LateNight_True_H_Graph <- SM_use_LateNight_True %>%
  ggplot() +
    geom_histogram(mapping=aes(x=Perceived_Stress_Score), bins = 40)

SM_use_LateNight_True_H_Graph

SM_use_LateNight_False_H_Graph <- SM_use_LateNight_False %>%
  ggplot() +
    geom_histogram(mapping=aes(x=Perceived_Stress_Score), bins = 40)

SM_use_LateNight_False_H_Graph

# shapiri-w tests
SM_use_True_SW_test <- shapiro.test(SM_use_LateNight_True$Perceived_Stress_Score)
SM_use_False_SW_test <-shapiro.test(SM_use_LateNight_False$Perceived_Stress_Score)

SM_use_True_SW_test
SM_use_False_SW_test
```

### Statistical comparison 
The data was not normally distributed according to both the histograms and the Shapiro-Wilk test, and I am comparing two groups, so I used a Wilcox test. 
```{r}
wilcox.test(Perceived_Stress_Score ~ Late_Night_Usage, data = SM_use)
```

###Conclusion
Here I assessed the perceived stress scores among individuals who did or did not report late night usage of social media. I used a Wilcox test as I was comparing two groups and the data was not normally distributed. The Wilcox test reported a p-value of less than .001, rejecting the null hypothesis that perceived stress score does not differ between groups that did and did not use social media late at night. These results indicate that those who use social media late at night have a higher perceived stress score. This conclusion carries the risk of being a type I error, or a false positive.
